correctness.rationale: The prior admissible-pair description yields \(c(P)=2J(P)-1+q(P)\), where \(J(P)\) is the number of ideals, equivalently antichains, and \(q(P)\) counts ordered nonempty antichain pairs \((X,Y)\) with every element of \(X\) below every element of \(Y\). Counting the empty antichain, all singletons and every incomparable pair gives \(J(P)\ge1+n+\operatorname{inc}(P)\), while singleton comparable pairs give \(q(P)\ge\operatorname{cmp}(P)\), proving the lower bound. For the upper bound, union maps every counted ordered pair injectively to a non-antichain subset because its minimal and maximal parts recover \(X,Y\), so \(q(P)\le2^n-J(P)\); together with \(J(P)\le2^n-\operatorname{cmp}(P)\) this gives the upper bound. Equality forces respectively no incomparable or no comparable pairs, hence the unique chain and antichain extrema. The package verifier enumerates finite posets through six points as a consistency check.

Dolinka--Mašulović provide the underlying lower-set/upper-set one-point extension structure. The new pair-sensitive inequalities then follow by counting singleton and two-point antichains/comparabilities and by the elementary union injection for \(q(P)\). Thus the unique endpoint classification and stability gaps are mechanically implied refinements of an already published stronger representation, not an independent scientific claim under the required implication standard.

final_claim: If \(P\) is the finite parameter poset of size \(n\) in the random poset and \(c(P)\) is its nonalgebraic one-point type count, then \(\binom{n+2}{2}+\operatorname{inc}(P)\le c(P)\le2^{n+1}-1-\operatorname{cmp}(P)\); consequently the chain uniquely minimizes and the antichain uniquely maximizes the complete 1-type count, with the displayed pair-sensitive stability gaps.
limitations: Finite parameter sets in the countable random poset only.
The result is mathematically correct but is an elementary extremal corollary of the previously published admissible-pair representation of one-point types.
